column6: Le gaspillage alimentaire est un vrai problème dans les cantines.
column7: Food waste is a real problem in canteens.
column8: Most often heard in «gaspillage alimentaire» (food waste). The related verb is «gaspiller».

column6: La cuisson des pâtes dure environ dix minutes.
column7: Cooking the pasta takes about ten minutes.
column8: It means the act of cooking food and is different from «cuisine». «Temps de cuisson» is the cooking time.

column6: Je fais fondre le chocolat dans une casserole à feu doux.
column7: I melt the chocolate in a saucepan over low heat.
column8: It is a pan with a long handle. In English «casserole» is a baked dish, so the two words do not match.

column6: Ma grand-mère prépare un ragoût de bœuf tous les dimanches.
column7: My grandmother makes a beef stew every Sunday.
column8: It means a slow-cooked stew of meat and vegetables. «Ragoût de bœuf» is a very common phrase.

column6: Je prépare la vinaigrette avec de l'huile d'olive et du vinaigre.
column7: I make the vinaigrette with olive oil and vinegar.
column8: It is the cold dressing for salad made with oil, vinegar and salt.

column6: Laissez un pourboire si le service vous a plu.
column7: Leave a tip if you liked the service.
column8: In France service is normally already included in the price, so the «pourboire» is optional.

column6: Nous avons demandé l'addition après le dessert.
column7: We asked for the bill after dessert.
column8: In a restaurant it means the bill; in maths it is the operation of adding.

column6: La nourriture de ce restaurant est toujours fraîche et copieuse.
column7: The food at this restaurant is always fresh and generous.
column8: It means food in general and is almost always used in the singular.

column6: Le riz est un aliment de base dans beaucoup de pays.
column7: Rice is a staple food in many countries.
column8: It means a food seen as nourishment. The adjective «alimentaire» means «food-related».

column6: Il faut laisser reposer la pâte pendant une heure.
column7: You have to let the dough rest for an hour.
column8: In the singular it means dough. In the plural «les pâtes» means pasta.

column6: Ajoutez de la levure à la farine.
column7: Add some yeast to the flour.
column8: «Levure chimique» is baking powder for cakes; «levure de boulanger» is baker's yeast for bread.

column6: Sers-moi une louche de soupe, s'il te plaît.
column7: Give me a ladle of soup, please.
column8: «Louche» is also an adjective meaning «shady», but as a feminine noun it is the ladle.

column6: Elle fait cuire les pommes de terre dans de la graisse d'oie.
column7: She cooks the potatoes in goose fat.
column8: It means both cooking fat and body fat. Labels use «matières grasses».

column6: Ce plat contient de la protéine végétale.
column7: This dish contains plant protein.
column8: It is written with an acute accent: «protéine».

column6: Elle surveille chaque calorie de son assiette.
column7: She watches every calorie on her plate.
column8: It is feminine («une calorie»). In diets people talk about «apport calorique» (calorie intake).

column6: Le basilic donne beaucoup de saveur à cette soupe.
column7: Basil gives this soup a lot of flavour.
column8: It is feminine («une saveur»). It stresses the particular flavour of a food.

column6: Le buffet du petit-déjeuner ouvre à sept heures.
column7: The breakfast buffet opens at seven o'clock.
column8: It means a self-service spread of food. It is also the word for a sideboard.

column6: Je reprendrai du bouillon, il est excellent.
column7: I will have more broth, it is excellent.
column8: A «cube de bouillon» is a stock cube.

column6: La serveuse apporte un plateau chargé de verres.
column7: The waitress brings a tray loaded with glasses.
column8: The plural is «plateaux». It also means plateau and a serving platter, as in «plateau de fromages».

column6: Nous avons réservé une dégustation de vins chez un viticulteur.
column7: We booked a wine tasting at a winemaker's.
column8: It is written with an acute accent. The related verb is «déguster».

column6: Trouver un logement abordable devient difficile dans les grandes villes.
column7: Finding affordable housing is becoming hard in big cities.
column8: It covers any place to live. «Crise du logement» is the housing crisis.

column6: Le locataire qui a signé le bail doit verser une caution.
column7: The tenant who signed the lease must pay a deposit.
column8: It is the same for masculine and feminine («le/la locataire»); «le» is given here by convention. It means the person renting.

column6: Les décisions de la copropriété sont prises en assemblée générale.
column7: The co-ownership's decisions are made at the general meeting.
column8: It is the system of jointly owned buildings, roughly like an Italian condominium.

column6: La perceuse dont j'ai besoin est dans la cave.
column7: The drill I need is in the cellar.
column8: It is the power drill. The related verb is «percer» (to drill a hole).

column6: Le marteau que tu cherches est resté dans le garage.
column7: The hammer you are looking for stayed in the garage.
column8: The plural is «marteaux», with an x.

column6: Il manque une vis pour monter cette étagère.
column7: One screw is missing to assemble this shelf.
column8: The final s is pronounced and the plural is identical. Do not confuse it with «vie» (life).

column6: Elle a enfoncé un clou dans le mur pour accrocher le cadre.
column7: She drove a nail into the wall to hang the frame.
column8: The plural is «clous». It appears in «clou de girofle» (clove).

column6: La peinture du salon commence à s'écailler près de la fenêtre.
column7: The paint in the living room is starting to flake near the window.
column8: It means both wall paint and the art of painting.

column6: La moquette de la chambre est usée et doit être remplacée.
column7: The bedroom carpet is worn and needs to be replaced.
column8: It is wall-to-wall carpeting. It differs from «tapis», a rug.

column6: Nous avons fait poncer le parquet avant d'emménager.
column7: We had the wooden floor sanded before moving in.
column8: The final t is silent. It also means the public prosecutor's office.

column6: La cloison derrière laquelle se trouve la chambre est très fine.
column7: The partition behind which the bedroom lies is very thin.
column8: It means an interior partition, thinner than a «mur».

column6: L'immeuble où nous habitons a une façade toute neuve.
column7: The building where we live has a brand-new facade.
column8: It is written with a cedilla «ç», pronounced /s/.

column6: Le voisinage s'est plaint du bruit de la fête.
column7: The neighbours complained about the noise of the party.
column8: It means the neighbours as a group and the area around the home. «Bon voisinage» is a set phrase.

column6: Nous faisons le ménage chaque samedi matin.
column7: We do the housework every Saturday morning.
column8: «Faire le ménage» means to clean the house. «Ménage» can also mean a household.

column6: Le repassage prend beaucoup de temps le dimanche soir.
column7: Ironing takes a lot of time on Sunday evening.
column8: The verb is «repasser» (to iron). An ironing board is a «planche à repasser».

column6: Il me faut un tournevis cruciforme pour ouvrir ce boîtier.
column7: I need a Phillips screwdriver to open this casing.
column8: It does not change in the plural: «des tournevis».

column6: Monte sur l'échelle avec prudence pour changer l'ampoule.
column7: Climb the ladder carefully to change the bulb.
column8: It also means a scale on a map or a rating. A staircase is «escalier».

column6: Une bonne isolation réduit la facture de chauffage.
column7: Good insulation lowers the heating bill.
column8: It is used for the thermal or sound insulation of a home («isolation thermique»).

column6: Le mobilier de ce studio est simple mais fonctionnel.
column7: The furniture in this studio is simple but functional.
column8: It is a singular collective noun for all the furniture, while «meuble» is a single piece.

column6: La colocation dans laquelle il vit compte quatre personnes.
column7: The flat-share he lives in has four people.
column8: Someone who shares the flat is a «colocataire»; the short, familiar form is «coloc».

column6: Le portail du jardin est resté ouvert toute la nuit.
column7: The garden gate stayed open all night.
column8: It means a large entrance gate. On the internet it is also a web portal. The plural is «portails».

column6: Mets les légumes au congélateur avant de partir.
column7: Put the vegetables in the freezer before leaving.
column8: The verb is «congeler». Industrially deep-frozen food is called «surgelé».

column6: Le consommateur a le droit d'être informé sur l'origine du produit.
column7: The consumer has the right to be informed about the origin of the product.
column8: The feminine is «consommatrice».

column6: La consommation d'énergie a baissé de dix pour cent.
column7: Energy consumption fell by ten percent.
column8: In cafes it also means a drink you ordered («une consommation»).

column6: Le commerçant m'a fait un rabais sur ce canapé abîmé.
column7: The shopkeeper gave me a discount on this damaged sofa.
column8: It means a discount granted on a price and is a synonym of «réduction». The final s is silent and the plural is unchanged.

column6: Cet appareil est encore sous garantie pour deux ans.
column7: This appliance is still under warranty for two years.
column8: «Être sous garantie» means a product is still covered.

column6: J'ai résilié mon abonnement à cette revue.
column7: I cancelled my subscription to this magazine.
column8: It is spelled with one b and two n's. The verb is «s'abonner».

column6: L'acheteur que le vendeur a rappelé n'a pas répondu.
column7: The buyer the seller called back did not answer.
column8: The feminine is «acheteuse». The related verb is «acheter».

column6: Le fournisseur chez lequel nous commandons livre en deux jours.
column7: The supplier we order from delivers within two days.
column8: «Fournisseur d'accès» is an internet service provider.

column6: Ils ont pris un crédit pour acheter leur première voiture.
column7: They took out a loan to buy their first car.
column8: Besides «credit», it often means a loan: «prendre un crédit» is to take out financing.

column6: Cet emprunt sera remboursé en vingt ans.
column7: This loan will be repaid over twenty years.
column8: It is the loan from the borrower's side; «prêt» is the lender's side.

column6: Elle a placé son épargne sur un compte à terme.
column7: She put her savings into a fixed-term account.
column8: Mostly used in the singular: «compte d'épargne»; «économies» is a different noun (always plural).

column6: Je vous ai envoyé un virement ce matin.
column7: I sent you a bank transfer this morning.
column8: «Faire un virement» is the usual phrase for making a bank transfer.

column6: Le distributeur est en panne, il faut retirer ailleurs.
column7: The cash machine is out of order, we have to withdraw elsewhere.
column8: «Distributeur de billets» is the cash machine and «distributeur automatique» is a vending machine.

column6: Le comptoir auquel vous devez vous adresser se trouve au fond.
column7: The counter you must go to is at the back.
column8: It means the counter of a shop or bar. «Au comptoir» means at the counter.

column6: L'euro est la devise de nombreux pays européens.
column7: The euro is the currency of many European countries.
column8: It means currency, but also the motto of a person or an institution.

column6: Le montant total figure en bas de la facture.
column7: The total amount appears at the bottom of the invoice.
column8: As a noun it means the amount of a sum. It is also the present participle of «monter».

column6: La taxe sur les boissons sucrées a augmenté cette année.
column7: The tax on sugary drinks went up this year.
column8: It is a charge on goods and services and is often distinguished from «impôt», tax in general such as income tax.

column6: L'entreprise a doublé son bénéfice grâce aux ventes en ligne.
column7: The company doubled its profit thanks to online sales.
column8: In business it is a company's profit. It also means «advantage», as in «au bénéfice de».

column6: La concurrence entre les magasins fait baisser les prix.
column7: Competition between shops brings prices down.
column8: A competitor is a «concurrent»; do not confuse it with «concours» (competitive exam).

column6: Il ne reste plus de stock pour cette taille.
column7: There is no stock left in this size.
column8: «En stock» means in stock and «rupture de stock» means sold out.

column6: La publicité qui passe avant le film dure dix minutes.
column7: The advertising shown before the film lasts ten minutes.
column8: In familiar speech it is shortened to «pub» (not the British bar).

column6: Il a fini par rembourser toute sa dette.
column7: He finally paid back all of his debt.
column8: It is spelled with two t's. «Dette publique» is public debt.

column6: Les consommateurs craignent une nouvelle hausse des prix.
column7: Consumers fear another rise in prices.
column8: The h is aspirate, so there is no elision: «la hausse». The opposite is «baisse».

column6: L'hébergement est compris dans le prix du séjour.
column7: Accommodation is included in the price of the stay.
column8: General term covering hotels, hostels and rented rooms.

column6: Nous avons raté la correspondance à cause du retard.
column7: We missed the connection because of the delay.
column8: It also means "correspondence" (an exchange of letters).

column6: Il faut demander un visa avant de partir en voyage.
column7: You have to apply for a visa before going on a trip.
column8: Masculine (un visa) and spelled with a single s.

column6: Le paysage que nous admirons depuis le train est magnifique.
column7: The landscape we are admiring from the train is magnificent.
column8: Masculine, like most nouns ending in -age.

column6: L'embarquement commence une heure avant le départ du vol.
column7: Boarding starts one hour before the flight departs.
column8: Used for planes, ships and ferries; the "carte d'embarquement" is the boarding pass.

column6: Cette excursion, à laquelle nous participons, part à huit heures.
column7: This excursion, which we are taking part in, leaves at eight o'clock.
column8: Means a short, often organised outing lasting a day or less.

column6: Le passager qui dort près de moi ronfle depuis une heure.
column7: The passenger sleeping next to me has been snoring for an hour.
column8: The feminine form is passagère.

column6: Le dépaysement est total quand on arrive dans un pays si différent.
column7: The change of scenery is total when you arrive in such a different country.
column8: Describes the feeling of being in a completely new environment, usually a positive one.

column6: Le décalage horaire m'a empêché de dormir la première nuit.
column7: The time difference kept me from sleeping the first night.
column8: In the phrase "décalage horaire" it means jet lag.

column6: Le voyagiste a annulé notre circuit à cause de la tempête.
column7: The tour operator cancelled our trip because of the storm.
column8: Same form for both genders (le/la voyagiste); "le" is given here as the more common article.

column6: Votre enregistrement en ligne est ouvert depuis hier soir.
column7: Your online check-in has been open since last night.
column8: It also means a sound or video "recording".

column6: Mon employeur propose le télétravail deux jours par semaine.
column7: My employer offers remote work two days a week.
column8: The feminine employeuse exists but is little used.

column6: Chaque salarié a droit à cinq semaines de congés payés.
column7: Every employee is entitled to five weeks of paid leave.
column8: The feminine is salariée; it refers to someone paid a wage, unlike the self-employed.

column6: Elle est devenue cadre dans une grande entreprise.
column7: She became a manager in a large company.
column8: It also means "frame"; for a woman one says "une cadre".

column6: Notre hiérarchie a validé le projet sans aucune modification.
column7: Our management has approved the project without any change.
column8: The h is silent, so the article elides: l'hiérarchie.

column6: C'est un investissement dont nous attendons beaucoup.
column7: It is an investment from which we expect a lot.
column8: It is written with a double s before «-ement»: investissement.

column6: La croissance économique ralentit depuis deux ans.
column7: Economic growth has been slowing for two years.
column8: Frequent collocation: croissance économique; the related verb is croître.

column6: Un actionnaire auquel j'ai parlé semblait très inquiet.
column7: A shareholder I spoke to seemed very worried.
column8: Same form for both genders; the article elides before it: l'actionnaire.

column6: La négociation avec les syndicats a duré toute la nuit.
column7: The negotiation with the unions lasted all night.
column8: Often used in the plural (les négociations) for formal talks.

column6: Nous devons respecter le délai fixé par le client.
column7: We must meet the deadline set by the client.
column8: False friend: it does not mean "delay" (retard) but the time allowed to do something.

column6: Notre objectif est d'augmenter les ventes de dix pour cent.
column7: Our goal is to increase sales by ten percent.
column8: It also means a camera "lens".

column6: Cette élection a été remportée par une large majorité.
column7: This election was won by a large majority.
column8: Often used in the plural: les élections.

column6: Chaque citoyen a le droit de voter à dix-huit ans.
column7: Every citizen has the right to vote at eighteen.
column8: The feminine is citoyenne; it stresses a person's civil and political rights.

column6: Ce reportage montre la vie quotidienne dans un hôpital.
column7: This report shows daily life in a hospital.
column8: Masculine; a press or television piece about an event or place.

column6: Le débat auquel j'ai assisté hier était passionnant.
column7: The debate I attended yesterday was fascinating.
column8: Masculine; the related verb is débattre.

column6: Cette loi sera votée au Parlement la semaine prochaine.
column7: This law will be voted on in Parliament next week.
column8: Means a law passed by parliament; law as a subject is "le droit".

column6: D'après ce sondage, la majorité soutient la réforme.
column7: According to this poll, the majority supports the reform.
column8: Often "sondage d'opinion"; the related verb is sonder.

column6: Cette émission est diffusée tous les jeudis soir.
column7: This programme is broadcast every Thursday evening.
column8: It also means "emission" (of gas, of money).

column6: Elle a obtenu son diplôme avec mention très bien.
column7: She earned her degree with a distinction.
column8: It is written with a circumflex accent on the o.

column6: La manifestation où nous allons part de la gare.
column7: The demonstration we are going to starts from the station.
column8: In French it mainly means a protest march, but also an event in general.

column6: Cette inégalité entre les régions se creuse depuis dix ans.
column7: This inequality between regions has been widening for ten years.
column8: Often used in the plural: les inégalités sociales.

column6: Ce mouvement artistique est apparu au début du siècle.
column7: This artistic movement appeared at the start of the century.
column8: Used for social, political and artistic movements as well as physical movement.

column6: La génération qui arrive sur le marché du travail est inquiète.
column7: The generation entering the job market is worried.
column8: Also used for a product model: la nouvelle génération.

column6: Le bénévole que vous cherchez est parti il y a dix minutes.
column7: The volunteer you are looking for left ten minutes ago.
column8: Same form for both genders (le/la bénévole).

column6: Cette collection, dont il est très fier, compte mille timbres.
column7: This collection, of which he is very proud, has a thousand stamps.
column8: The related verb is collectionner.

column6: Le randonneur a suivi le sentier balisé jusqu'au refuge.
column7: The hiker followed the marked trail to the hut.
column8: The feminine is randonneuse.

column6: Notre champion a battu le record du monde hier.
column7: Our champion broke the world record yesterday.
column8: The feminine is championne, with a double n.

column6: Il s'entraîne depuis un an pour cette compétition.
column7: He has been training for a year for this competition.
column8: Used for sporting contests; in economics concurrence is preferred.

column6: Cette escalade nous a pris quatre heures.
column7: This climb took us four hours.
column8: It can also mean "escalation": l'escalade de la violence.

column6: Après cette semaine, j'ai besoin de détente.
column7: After this week, I need some relaxation.
column8: It also means an easing of tension between two countries.

column6: Le cinéma reste mon divertissement préféré.
column7: Cinema remains my favourite form of entertainment.
column8: Linked to the verb se divertir (to enjoy oneself).

column6: La séance de cinéma commence à vingt heures.
column7: The film screening starts at eight p.m.
column8: It also means a work or therapy session: séance de travail.

column6: Une bonne hygiène bucco-dentaire évite beaucoup de problèmes.
column7: Good oral hygiene avoids many problems.
column8: The h is silent, so the article elides: l'hygiène.

column6: Une carence en fer provoque souvent de la fatigue.
column7: An iron deficiency often causes tiredness.
column8: In medicine it means a lack of a substance: carence en vitamines.

column6: Sa rééducation après l'opération dure trois mois.
column7: His rehabilitation after the operation lasts three months.
column8: Used for physiotherapy after injuries or operations.

column6: Cette urgence médicale demande une intervention immédiate.
column7: This medical emergency requires immediate intervention.
column8: In the plural, "les urgences" means the hospital emergency room.

column6: Le stress au travail peut provoquer des insomnies.
column7: Stress at work can cause insomnia.
column8: A loan from English, masculine; spelled with a double s.

column6: Le dépistage précoce permet de soigner la maladie.
column7: Early screening makes it possible to treat the disease.
column8: A test to detect an illness before symptoms appear.

column6: Cette épidémie s'est propagée en quelques semaines.
column7: This epidemic spread within a few weeks.
column8: Used for a disease spreading through a region or population.

column6: Cette infection est traitée avec des antibiotiques.
column7: This infection is treated with antibiotics.
column8: It is spelled with -ct-: infection.

column6: Cette thérapie donne de bons résultats chez les jeunes.
column7: This therapy gives good results in young people.
column8: Also used for psychotherapy: faire une thérapie.

column6: Cette blessure peut laisser une séquelle.
column7: This injury can leave a lasting effect.
column8: Almost always used in the plural: les séquelles.

column6: Elle a décidé d'étudier la médecine à Paris.
column7: She decided to study medicine in Paris.
column8: It means the discipline; the drug is called médicament.

column6: Cette opération se fait sous anesthésie locale.
column7: This operation is done under local anaesthesia.
column8: It is spelled with -th-: anesthésie.

column6: Elle a amélioré sa recette de soupe.
column7: She improved her soup recipe.
column8: Regular -er verb; its passé composé takes avoir.

column6: Vous avez défini les règles du jeu.
column7: You defined the rules of the game.
column8: Regular -ir verb like finir: nous définissons, past participle défini.

column6: Elle a accompli sa mission sans aide.
column7: She accomplished her mission without help.
column8: Regular -ir verb: nous accomplissons, past participle accompli.

column6: Il a consulté un spécialiste la semaine dernière.
column7: He consulted a specialist last week.
column8: Also used for doctors: consulter un médecin means to see a doctor.

column6: Nous avons comparé les prix de trois magasins.
column7: We compared the prices of three shops.
column8: It is used as comparer A à B or comparer A avec B.

column6: Notre voisin est décédé l'an dernier.
column7: Our neighbour passed away last year.
column8: Formal verb used for people; its passé composé takes être.

column6: Ils ont photographié le village depuis la colline.
column7: They photographed the village from the hill.
column8: Verb in -ier: the imperfect is nous photographiions, with two i.

column6: Tu as commenté mon article sans le lire.
column7: You commented on my article without reading it.
column8: It takes a direct object: commenter un article, with no preposition.

column6: Il faut que nous économisions de l'argent.
column7: We need to save money.
column8: Il faut que is followed by the subjunctive: que nous économisions.

column6: Il faut que vous surveilliez la cuisson du riz.
column7: You must keep an eye on the cooking of the rice.
column8: In the subjunctive nous and vous take -iions and -iez: que vous surveilliez.

column6: Il faut que tu consommes moins de sel.
column7: You need to consume less salt.
column8: Regular -er verb; the noun is la consommation.

column6: Il faut que vous exerciez votre mémoire chaque jour.
column7: You need to exercise your memory every day.
column8: Before a and o it takes a cedilla: nous exerçons.

column6: Il faut que nous corrigions ces erreurs avant lundi.
column7: We need to correct these mistakes before Monday.
column8: Before a and o it is spelled -ge-: nous corrigeons.

column6: Il faut que ce billet corresponde à votre nom.
column7: This ticket must match your name.
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre; it takes the preposition à.

column6: Il faut que vous révisiez cette leçon avant l'examen.
column7: You need to revise this lesson before the exam.
column8: It also means to service or to review, for example a car or a text.

column6: Il faut que les citoyens votent demain.
column7: Citizens must vote tomorrow.
column8: Regular -er verb; you say voter pour someone.

column6: Il faut que vous suspendiez ce rideau plus haut.
column7: You need to hang this curtain higher.
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre; it also means to suspend.

column6: Je ne veux pas que vous stationniez devant la porte.
column7: I do not want you to park in front of the door.
column8: Regular -er verb; used for parking a vehicle.

column6: Il faut que nous cultivions notre jardin.
column7: We must cultivate our garden.
column8: It is also used figuratively: cultiver son esprit.

column6: Il est impossible que nous tolérions ce retard de livraison.
column7: It is impossible for us to tolerate this delivery delay.
column8: The accent changes in the present: je tolère, but nous tolérons.

column6: Elle avait déjà confirmé notre réservation.
column7: She had already confirmed our reservation.
column8: Regular -er verb with a direct object: confirmer une réservation.

column6: Il avait trahi la confiance de ses collègues.
column7: He had betrayed his colleagues' trust.
column8: Regular -ir verb like finir: nous trahissons.

column6: La neige avait fondu avant midi.
column7: The snow had melted before noon.
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre; past participle fondu.

column6: Nous avions déjà dégusté ce fromage.
column7: We had already tasted this cheese.
column8: False friend: déguster means to savour, not to disgust.

column6: Ce film avait inspiré plusieurs romans célèbres.
column7: This film had inspired several famous novels.
column8: It also means to breathe in.

column6: Le magasin nous avait déjà remboursé la veste.
column7: The shop had already refunded us for the jacket.
column8: Regular -er verb; the noun is le remboursement.

column6: L'infirmière avait déjà vacciné tous les enfants.
column7: The nurse had already vaccinated all the children.
column8: You also say se faire vacciner contre une maladie.

column6: Ils avaient préservé le vieux four de leur grand-mère.
column7: They had preserved their grandmother's old oven.
column8: It is also used with de: préserver quelqu'un de quelque chose.

column6: Beaucoup d'argent a été investi dans ce projet.
column7: A lot of money was invested in this project.
column8: Regular -ir verb: nous investissons, past participle investi.

column6: Le château a été restauré l'an dernier.
column7: The castle was restored last year.
column8: Used for monuments and works of art; the noun is la restauration.

column6: Les cadeaux ont été emballés avec soin.
column7: The gifts were wrapped with care.
column8: The opposite is déballer, to unwrap.

column6: Le patient a été opéré hier soir.
column7: The patient was operated on last night.
column8: The accent changes in the present: il opère, but nous opérons.

column6: Le raisin a été récolté en septembre.
column7: The grapes were harvested in September.
column8: Used for crops, but also figuratively: récolter des applaudissements.

column6: Notre vol a été retardé de deux heures.
column7: Our flight was delayed by two hours.
column8: The noun is le retard.

column6: Le vieil immeuble a été démoli en mars.
column7: The old building was demolished in March.
column8: Regular -ir verb like finir: nous démolissons.

column6: Le match a été diffusé en direct.
column7: The match was broadcast live.
column8: Used for tv and radio broadcasts, and for spreading news.

column6: Il a dit qu'il renoncerait au voyage.
column7: He said he would give up the trip.
column8: It takes à; before a and o it takes a cedilla: nous renonçons.

column6: Elle a dit qu'elle insisterait auprès du directeur.
column7: She said she would insist with the director.
column8: Used with sur something or pour plus an infinitive.

column6: Mon frère a dit qu'il déménagerait en mars.
column7: My brother said he would move house in March.
column8: Before a and o it is spelled -ge-: nous déménageons.

column6: Le médecin a dit qu'il recommanderait un peu de repos.
column7: The doctor said he would recommend some rest.
column8: A lettre recommandée is a registered letter.

column6: Il a dit qu'il mijoterait le ragoût pendant deux heures.
column7: He said he would simmer the stew for two hours.
column8: A cooking verb: to cook slowly over low heat.

column6: Le vendeur a dit qu'il garantirait l'appareil deux ans.
column7: The seller said he would guarantee the appliance for two years.
column8: Regular -ir verb: nous garantissons.

column6: Tu assisterais volontiers à ce concert.
column7: You would gladly attend this concert.
column8: False friend: assister à means to be present at; to help is aider.

column6: Nous fréquenterions ce café plus souvent.
column7: We would go to this café more often.
column8: Fréquenter someone can also mean to be dating them.

column6: Ils bâtiraient une maison près du lac.
column7: They would build a house near the lake.
column8: Regular -ir verb: nous bâtissons; it is less common than construire.

column6: Vous négocieriez un meilleur salaire.
column7: You would negotiate a better salary.
column8: Verb in -ier: nous négocions, que nous négociions.

column6: Ce sirop calmerait ta toux rapidement.
column7: This syrup would soothe your cough quickly.
column8: Used with an object (calmer la toux) or reflexively: se calmer.

column6: Nous embarquerions à huit heures.
column7: We would board at eight o'clock.
column8: Used for ships and planes; the opposite is débarquer.

column6: Nous étendrons le linge dehors demain.
column7: We will hang the laundry outside tomorrow.
column8: Regular -re verb like vendre; past participle étendu.

column6: Nous explorerons cette région à vélo.
column7: We will explore this region by bike.
column8: Regular -er verb with a direct object.

column6: Nous grillerons les poissons ce soir.
column7: We will grill the fish tonight.
column8: Informally, griller un feu rouge means to run a red light.

column6: Tu soulageras ta douleur avec ce médicament.
column7: You will relieve your pain with this medicine.
column8: Before a and o it is spelled -ge-: nous soulageons.

column6: Le match dépendra de la météo.
column7: The match will depend on the weather.
column8: It takes de: dépendre de quelque chose.

column6: Le dimanche, mon père pêchait au bord du lac.
column7: On Sundays my father fished by the lake.
column8: Do not confuse it with pécher, which means to sin.

column6: Quand j'étais petit, ma mère tricotait des pulls.
column7: When I was little, my mother knitted sweaters.
column8: Regular -er verb; the noun is le tricot.

column6: À cette époque, il dirigeait une petite usine.
column7: At that time he managed a small factory.
column8: Before a and o it is spelled -ge-: il dirigeait, nous dirigeons.

column6: Il toussait toute la nuit.
column7: He coughed all night.
column8: The noun is la toux.

column6: Elle se concentre sur son travail.
column7: She concentrates on her work.
column8: Used reflexively: se concentrer sur means to concentrate on.

column6: Nous nous adaptons vite à ce climat.
column7: We adapt quickly to this climate.
column8: Used reflexively with à: s'adapter à.

column6: Ils se débrouillent bien en cuisine.
column7: They manage well in the kitchen.
column8: Used reflexively: se débrouiller means to get by.

column6: Ne vous approchez pas de la voie.
column7: Do not go near the tracks.
column8: Used reflexively with de: s'approcher de.

column6: Nous nous rappelons encore cette belle soirée.
column7: We still remember that lovely evening.
column8: Se rappeler quelque chose takes a direct object, without de.

column6: Il se rase tous les matins.
column7: He shaves every morning.
column8: Used reflexively: se raser means to shave oneself.

column6: Nous devons conclure cet accord avant vendredi.
column7: We must conclude this agreement before Friday.
column8: Irregular: je conclus, nous concluons; past participle conclu.

column6: Le prix peut inclure le petit-déjeuner.
column7: The price may include breakfast.
column8: Conjugated like conclure; the past participle is inclus.

column6: Il faut parcourir trente kilomètres à pied.
column7: You have to cover thirty kilometres on foot.
column8: Conjugated like courir; the past participle is parcouru.

column6: Il faut accueillir nos amis à la maison.
column7: We must welcome our friends at home.
column8: Conjugated like cueillir: j'accueille, nous accueillons.

column6: Il faut entretenir régulièrement la chaudière.
column7: The boiler must be looked after regularly.
column8: Conjugated like tenir; it also means to entertain a conversation.

column6: Il faut maintenir le poisson au frais.
column7: You must keep the fish cool.
column8: Conjugated like tenir; the past participle is maintenu.

column6: Ce tableau doit appartenir à un collectionneur.
column7: This painting must belong to a collector.
column8: It takes à; conjugated like tenir.

column6: Ce sirop ne doit pas contenir d'alcool.
column7: This syrup must not contain alcohol.
column8: Conjugated like tenir; the past participle is contenu.

column6: Ils veulent détruire ce vieux mur.
column7: They want to tear down this old wall.
column8: Conjugated like construire; the past participle is détruit.

column6: Nous voulons réduire nos dépenses mensuelles.
column7: We want to reduce our monthly spending.
column8: Conjugated like construire; the past participle is réduit.

column6: Il faut couvrir la casserole pendant dix minutes.
column7: You must cover the pot for ten minutes.
column8: Conjugated like ouvrir: je couvre; past participle couvert.

column6: Le patient ne doit pas mentir à son médecin.
column7: The patient must not lie to his doctor.
column8: Conjugated like partir: je mens, nous mentons.

column6: Il est facile de commettre cette erreur.
column7: It is easy to make this mistake.
column8: Conjugated like mettre; the past participle is commis.

column6: Le guide sait transmettre sa passion de l'histoire.
column7: The guide knows how to pass on his passion for history.
column8: Conjugated like mettre; the past participle is transmis.

column6: Elle veut entreprendre un long voyage en Asie.
column7: She wants to undertake a long journey in Asia.
column8: Conjugated like prendre; the past participle is entrepris.

column6: Notre équipe veut battre le champion samedi.
column7: Our team wants to beat the champion on Saturday.
column8: In the singular it has a single t: je bats, il bat; past participle battu.

column6: Il faut vaincre sa peur de l'avion.
column7: You have to overcome your fear of flying.
column8: Irregular: je vaincs, nous vainquons; past participle vaincu.

column6: Ils ont décidé de rompre le contrat.
column7: They decided to break off the contract.
column8: Conjugated like vendre, but the third person is il rompt; past participle rompu.

column6: Beaucoup de touristes veulent fuir la chaleur.
column7: Many tourists want to escape the heat.
column8: Irregular: je fuis, nous fuyons; past participle fui.

column6: Cet architecte sait concevoir des maisons écologiques.
column7: This architect knows how to design eco-friendly houses.
column8: Conjugated like recevoir; the past participle is conçu.

column6: Je ne veux pas décevoir mes clients.
column7: I do not want to disappoint my customers.
column8: Conjugated like recevoir; the past participle is déçu.

column6: Elle doit parvenir à dormir plus longtemps.
column7: She must manage to sleep longer.
column8: Conjugated like venir, with the auxiliary être; it takes à.

column6: Il est difficile de retenir tous ces mots.
column7: It is hard to memorize all these words.
column8: Conjugated like tenir; it also means to hold back or to reserve.

column6: Un bon dictionnaire est indispensable pour ce travail.
column7: A good dictionary is essential for this work.
column8: Same form in masculine and feminine; plural indispensables.

column6: Ce médicament est très efficace contre la toux.
column7: This medicine is very effective against coughs.
column8: Same form in masculine and feminine; plural efficaces.

column6: La photo est floue, on ne voit presque rien.
column7: The photo is blurry, you can hardly see anything.
column8: Feminine floue; used for images and also for unclear ideas.

column6: Cette application est fiable et facile à utiliser.
column7: This app is reliable and easy to use.
column8: Same form in both genders; said of people, sources and machines.

column6: Elle achète des vêtements durables pour polluer moins.
column7: She buys durable clothes in order to pollute less.
column8: In développement durable it means sustainable; same form in both genders.

column6: Mon patron propose des horaires souples.
column7: My boss offers flexible working hours.
column8: Same form in both genders; applies to objects, people and schedules.

column6: Le salon est vaste et très lumineux.
column7: The living room is vast and very bright.
column8: Same form in both genders; usually describes a large surface or area.

column6: Ce vin est rare et assez cher.
column7: This wine is rare and quite expensive.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural rares.

column6: Le réseau est faible dans cette vallée.
column7: The signal is weak in this valley.
column8: Same form in both genders; also used for a small amount (un faible revenu).

column6: J'ai lu un article récent sur ce sujet.
column7: I read a recent article on this subject.
column8: Feminine récente; the first e carries an acute accent.

column6: La solution est évidente pour tout le monde.
column7: The solution is obvious to everyone.
column8: Feminine évidente; means obvious or clear.

column6: Les retards sont fréquents sur cette ligne.
column7: Delays are frequent on this line.
column8: Feminine fréquente; describes events that happen often.

column6: Il y a une erreur flagrante dans ce contrat.
column7: There is a blatant mistake in this contract.
column8: Feminine flagrante; often describes a mistake or an injustice.

column6: Son humour est subtil et jamais méchant.
column7: His humour is subtle and never mean.
column8: Feminine subtile; used figuratively, for thin objects French uses mince or fin.

column6: Donnez-moi un exemple concret, s'il vous plaît.
column7: Give me a concrete example, please.
column8: Feminine concrète; the opposite of abstrait.

column6: Cette peinture est trop abstraite pour moi.
column7: This painting is too abstract for me.
column8: Feminine abstraite; opposite of concret.

column6: Le coût global du voyage reste raisonnable.
column7: The overall cost of the trip remains reasonable.
column8: Plural globaux, feminine globale; often means overall.

column6: Cette chercheuse est très rigoureuse dans son travail.
column7: This researcher is very rigorous in her work.
column8: Feminine rigoureuse; said of weather it means harsh (un hiver rigoureux).

column6: Elle a un projet ambitieux pour sa boutique.
column7: She has an ambitious plan for her shop.
column8: Feminine ambitieuse; written -tieux but pronounced /sjø/.

column6: Soyez prudents sur la route ce soir.
column7: Be careful on the road tonight.
column8: Feminine prudente; plural prudents.

column6: Le vendeur est honnête et très aimable.
column7: The seller is honest and very kind.
column8: Same form in both genders; with a price it means fair or reasonable.

column6: Ce restaurant a une clientèle fidèle.
column7: This restaurant has a loyal clientele.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural fidèles.

column6: Le service était médiocre hier soir.
column7: The service was poor last night.
column8: Same form in both genders; more negative than moyen.

column6: Cette explication me paraît plausible.
column7: This explanation seems plausible to me.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural plausibles.

column6: Ce bijou est précieux pour ma famille.
column7: This piece of jewellery is precious to my family.
column8: Feminine précieuse; also said of time and advice.

column6: Cette table est solide et belle.
column7: This table is sturdy and beautiful.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural solides.

column6: Il cherche un emploi stable.
column7: He is looking for a stable job.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural stables.

column6: Le médecin est strict sur mon régime.
column7: The doctor is strict about my diet.
column8: Feminine stricte; the final t is pronounced.

column6: Le cuisinier, minutieux, pèse chaque ingrédient.
column7: The cook, meticulous, weighs every ingredient.
column8: Feminine minutieuse; implies attention to detail.

column6: Après l'accident, elle est restée lucide.
column7: After the accident, she stayed lucid.
column8: Same form in both genders; describes someone thinking clearly.

column6: Ils habitent dans un modeste appartement.
column7: They live in a modest flat.
column8: Same form in both genders; can precede the noun and may also mean of limited means.

column6: Il est trop naïf pour ce métier.
column7: He is too naive for this job.
column8: Feminine naïve; the i carries a diaeresis.

column6: Mon grand-père est obstiné et refuse de se reposer.
column7: My grandfather is stubborn and refuses to rest.
column8: Feminine obstinée; a participle used as an adjective.

column6: Le prix de cet hôtel est raisonnable.
column7: The price of this hotel is reasonable.
column8: Same form in both genders; written with two n.

column6: Cette boutique n'est pas encore rentable.
column7: This shop is not yet profitable.
column8: Same form in both genders; said of a business that makes money.

column6: Elle a la peau sensible au soleil.
column7: Her skin is sensitive to the sun.
column8: False friend: it means sensitive, not sensible (that is sensé).

column6: Cette quantité est suffisante pour six personnes.
column7: This amount is sufficient for six people.
column8: Feminine suffisante; said of a person it can mean self-satisfied.

column6: Sa réponse est restée vague.
column7: His answer remained vague.
column8: Same form in both genders; as a noun la vague means wave.

column6: Boire de l'eau est vital en été.
column7: Drinking water is vital in summer.
column8: Feminine vitale, plural vitaux.

column6: Le succès de cette chanson fut éphémère.
column7: The success of this song was short-lived.
column8: Same form in both genders; plural éphémères.

column6: Le tabac est nuisible pour la santé.
column7: Tobacco is harmful to health.
column8: Same form in both genders; used with à or pour.

column6: Nos voisins sont tolérants avec le bruit.
column7: Our neighbours are tolerant about noise.
column8: Feminine tolérante; plural tolérants.

column6: Le concert était long ; néanmoins, il était magnifique.
column7: The concert was long; nevertheless, it was magnificent.
column8: Rather formal and more common in writing; it introduces a contrast.

column6: Mon français est nettement meilleur cette année.
column7: My French is markedly better this year.
column8: It strengthens a comparative (nettement plus, nettement mieux) or means clearly.

column6: Auparavant, nous habitions dans un petit village.
column7: Previously, we lived in a small village.
column8: Used on its own with no complement, unlike avant.

column6: Ainsi, nous n'arriverons pas en retard.
column7: This way, we will not arrive late.
column8: At the start of a sentence it introduces a consequence; with que it forms ainsi que.

column6: Appelez-moi, et je viendrai aussitôt.
column7: Call me, and I will come immediately.
column8: Written with a circumflex on the o; a synonym of tout de suite.

column6: Autrefois, on voyageait surtout en train.
column7: In the past, people mostly travelled by train.
column8: Usually found with the imparfait and refers to a distant past.

column6: Apparemment, le magasin est fermé le lundi.
column7: Apparently, the shop is closed on Mondays.
column8: Like other -emment adverbs it is pronounced /amɑ̃/ and has two m.

column6: Évidemment, je serais ravi de venir.
column7: Obviously, I would be delighted to come.
column8: Like other -emment adverbs it is pronounced /amɑ̃/; often means of course.

column6: Il viendra certainement à la fête.
column7: He will certainly come to the party.
column8: Expresses strong likelihood or a polite yes.

column6: Le vol aura vraisemblablement du retard.
column7: The flight will most likely be delayed.
column8: Rather formal; built on the adjective vraisemblable.

column6: C'est précisément le livre que je cherchais.
column7: It is precisely the book I was looking for.
column8: Often emphasises an identification, like exactly.

column6: Actuellement, mon frère est au chômage.
column7: Currently, my brother is unemployed.
column8: False friend: it means currently, not actually (that is en fait).

column6: Je pourrais éventuellement t'aider ce soir.
column7: I could possibly help you tonight.
column8: False friend for English speakers: it does not mean eventually (that is finalement).

column6: Effectivement, la facture était plus élevée.
column7: Indeed, the bill was higher.
column8: Used to confirm someone's remark or a fact.

column6: D'ailleurs, il n'y a pas de bus le dimanche.
column7: Besides, there is no bus on Sundays.
column8: Adds an extra point or remark; it does not mean elsewhere.

column6: Pendant la randonnée, le ciel s'était subitement assombri.
column7: During the hike, the sky had suddenly darkened.
column8: Built on the adjective subit; soudain is also common.

column6: Nous n'avons pas autant de temps aujourd'hui.
column7: We do not have as much time today.
column8: Used with de before a noun (autant de temps) to express equal quantity.

column6: Tantôt il est joyeux, tantôt il est triste.
column7: Sometimes he is cheerful, sometimes he is sad.
column8: Usually repeated in a pair (tantôt... tantôt) for two alternating situations.

column6: Ce projet est difficile, voire impossible.
column7: This project is difficult, even impossible.
column8: Strengthens what came before with a stronger term; invariable.

column6: Il est très poli envers les clients.
column7: He is very polite toward customers.
column8: Used for attitudes and feelings, not for movement.

column6: Hormis le dessert, tout était délicieux.
column7: Apart from the dessert, everything was delicious.
column8: Formal, more common in writing; used before a noun.

column6: Concernant votre commande, elle sera livrée demain.
column7: Regarding your order, it will be delivered tomorrow.
column8: Administrative and business register; invariable.

column6: Nous allons voyager via Lyon cette fois.
column7: We are going to travel via Lyon this time.
column8: Indicates a route or a means (via e-mail); invariable.

column6: Outre le loyer, vous paierez les charges.
column7: Besides the rent, you will pay the service charges.
column8: Rather formal; used before a noun to add something.

column6: Tout le monde sera là, excepté mon oncle.
column7: Everyone will be there, except my uncle.
column8: Invariable before the noun; it agrees when placed after it (ma sœur exceptée).

column6: Les chambres sont moins chères hors saison.
column7: Rooms are cheaper off-season.
column8: Used without de in expressions such as hors taxes and hors saison.

column6: Tous les magasins étaient fermés ; or nous avions besoin de pain.
column7: All the shops were closed; yet we needed bread.
column8: Introduces a fact leading to a contrast or conclusion; as a noun or means gold.

column6: Quiconque est en retard doit attendre dehors.
column7: Anyone who is late must wait outside.
column8: Invariable and masculine singular; often used in rules and notices.

column6: Voici le projet auquel je pense depuis longtemps.
column7: Here is the project I have been thinking about for a long time.
column8: Contraction of à plus lequel; feminine à laquelle, plural auxquels and auxquelles.

column6: Chacune de ces recettes est facile.
column7: Each of these recipes is easy.
column8: Feminine of chacun; it replaces a feminine noun.

column6: Ceux qui aiment la randonnée adorent cette région.
column7: Those who like hiking love this region.
column8: Masculine plural of celui; usually followed by qui, que or de.

column6: Cette veste est celle que je préfère.
column7: This jacket is the one I prefer.
column8: Feminine of celui; plural celles; usually followed by qui, que or de.

column6: Les amis avec lesquels je voyage sont italiens.
column7: The friends with whom I travel are Italian.
column8: Used after a preposition; feminine lesquelles; with à and de it becomes auxquels and desquels.

column6: Voici le village près duquel nous campons.
column7: Here is the village near which we are camping.
column8: Contraction of de plus lequel; feminine de laquelle and plural desquels.

column6: Tous étaient fatigués après la longue randonnée.
column7: Everyone was tired after the long hike.
column8: As a pronoun the final s is pronounced, as an adjective it is not.

column6: Quoique je sois fatigué, je vais danser.
column7: Although I am tired, I am going to dance.
column8: It takes the subjunctive (je sois). Not to be confused with quoi que, written as two words.

column6: L'enjeu de cette élection est considérable.
column7: The stakes of this election are considerable.
column8: It is often used in the plural: «les enjeux».

column6: Apprendre une langue est un beau défi.
column7: Learning a language is a great challenge.
column8: You say «relever un défi» for «to take up a challenge».

column6: Chaque déchet doit être trié.
column7: Every item of waste must be sorted.
column8: In everyday speech it is mostly used in the plural: «les déchets».

column6: Ce contrat offre un grand avantage.
column7: This contract offers a big advantage.
column8: The opposite is «inconvénient».

column6: Cette solution présente un inconvénient majeur.
column7: This solution has a major drawback.
column8: It is often paired with «avantage»: «avantages et inconvénients».

column6: Cette tendance vient de Paris.
column7: This trend comes from Paris.
column8: It is used for fashion («être tendance») and for statistics («tendance à la hausse»).

column6: La fatigue est une conséquence fréquente de cette maladie.
column7: Tiredness is a frequent consequence of this illness.
column8: You say «en conséquence» for «as a result».

column6: Personne ne connaît l'ampleur du problème.
column7: Nobody knows the extent of the problem.
column8: It is used almost only in the singular: «prendre de l'ampleur».

column6: Il exige que nous soyons à l'heure.
column7: He demands that we be on time.
column8: It is followed by the subjunctive: «exiger que» + subjunctive.

column6: La grève nous a empêchés de partir.
column7: The strike prevented us from leaving.
column8: It takes «de» + infinitive: «empêcher quelqu'un de».

column6: Je souhaite que vous réussissiez.
column7: I hope you succeed.
column8: With «que» it takes the subjunctive; it is more formal than «vouloir».

column6: Il affirme qu'il n'était pas là.
column7: He claims he was not there.
column8: It introduces a firm statement; with «que» + indicative.

column6: Les mentalités ont beaucoup évolué.
column7: Attitudes have changed a lot.
column8: It is used for gradual change over time.

column6: Le directeur souligne l'importance du projet.
column7: The director stresses the importance of the project.
column8: It means both to underline with a pen and to emphasise.

column6: Nous envisageons de déménager l'année prochaine.
column7: We are considering moving next year.
column8: It takes «de» + infinitive.

column6: Elle évoque ses souvenirs d'enfance.
column7: She recalls her childhood memories.
column8: It is more formal than «parler de».

column6: Le journal dénonce ces abus.
column7: The newspaper denounces these abuses.
column8: It does not only mean reporting to the police: it also means criticising publicly.

column6: Il a surmonté toutes ses peurs.
column7: He overcame all his fears.
column8: It is used for obstacles, fears and difficulties.

column6: Cette remarque est très pertinente.
column7: This remark is very relevant.
column8: It is used for arguments and questions; it is formal.

column6: Cette conséquence était inévitable.
column7: This consequence was unavoidable.
column8: It has the same form for masculine and feminine.

column6: Il est certes cher, mais il est solide.
column7: It is admittedly expensive, but it is solid.
column8: It introduces a concession, usually followed by «mais».

column6: La récolte de cette année a souffert de la sécheresse.
column7: This year's harvest suffered from the drought.
column8: It means both the act of gathering and the crop itself; for cereals "moisson" is often used.

column6: Il a perdu l'appétit depuis quelques jours.
column7: He has lost his appetite over the last few days.
column8: Bon appétit is the phrase used before a meal; figuratively it can also mean a strong drive.

column6: Son adolescence a été marquée par de nombreux déménagements.
column7: His adolescence was marked by many moves.
column8: It is spelled with "sc" as in English and the "sc" sounds like a plain "s".

column6: Cette assurance couvre les dégâts des eaux et le vol.
column7: This insurance covers water damage and theft.
column8: It also means self-confidence (avoir de l'assurance).

column6: Voici le sentier par lequel nous sommes redescendus hier soir.
column7: Here is the path by which we came back down last night.
column8: A narrow track, mostly in the countryside or mountains; narrower than a road or a lane.

column6: Il faut retirer les billets au guichet de la gare.
column7: You must collect the tickets at the station window.
column8: An opening or counter where customers are served (station, bank, post office); « à guichets fermés » means sold out.

column6: Le ministre a prononcé un discours très applaudi.
column7: The minister gave a much-applauded speech.
column8: The word is unchanged in the plural and the final s is silent; one « prononce » or « tient » a discours.

column6: Elle fait du yoga chaque matin avant de travailler.
column7: She does yoga every morning before working.
column8: One says « faire du yoga »; the word is masculine.

column6: La plongée sous-marine exige une bonne condition physique.
column7: Scuba diving requires good physical fitness.
column8: The activity of going down under water; either « plongée libre » (breath-hold) or with a tank.

column6: Ils ont loué un voilier pour la semaine.
column7: They rented a sailboat for the week.
column8: A boat driven by sails; different from a motorboat.

column6: Le tricot l'aide à se détendre le soir.
column7: Knitting helps her relax in the evening.
column8: Refers to the activity or the work done with needles; the word can also mean a sweater.

column6: Après le déjeuner, il fait une courte sieste.
column7: After lunch, he takes a short nap.
column8: One « fait la sieste »; the word means a short rest after the midday meal.

column6: Il s'entraîne depuis six mois pour le marathon.
column7: He has been training for six months for the marathon.
column8: A footrace of over forty kilometres; the word is also used figuratively for a very long ordeal.

column6: Vous avez mesuré chaque étagère avant d'acheter les meubles.
column7: You measured every shelf before buying the furniture.
column8: Transitive; also used figuratively, as in mesurer un risque.

column6: Il faut que nous abandonnions ce vieux canapé avant le déménagement.
column7: We have to give up this old sofa before the move.
column8: Transitive: abandonner un projet; it also means to leave someone behind.

column6: Il faut que nous revendions ces billets de concert avant vendredi.
column7: We have to resell these concert tickets before Friday.
column8: A regular -re verb, conjugated like vendre.

column6: À ta place, je ne mordrais pas dans ce fruit vert.
column7: If I were you, I would not bite into this green fruit.
column8: A regular -re verb, conjugated like vendre; it takes mordre dans quelque chose.

column6: Le magasin est quasiment vide le mardi matin.
column7: The shop is almost empty on Tuesday mornings.
column8: A synonym of presque, very common. It usually stands before the adjective or verb it modifies.

column6: Si tu parlais couramment allemand, tu obtiendrais ce poste.
column7: If you spoke German fluently, you would get this job.
column8: With parler it means speaking a language fluently; it also means commonly (s'emploie couramment).

column6: Je voulais justement t'appeler pour ce week-end.
column7: I was just about to call you about this weekend.
column8: In speech it stresses a coincidence (j'allais justement le dire); it can also mean rightly.

column6: Elle sera guérie dans une semaine, d'après le médecin.
column7: She will be better in a week, according to the doctor.
column8: The word contains an apostrophe (d'après). It introduces a source of information or a model (d'après une histoire vraie).

column6: La marchandise a été livrée avec trois semaines de retard.
column7: The goods were delivered three weeks late.
column8: What is sold; often singular as a collective, while «marchandises» is also common.

column6: L'assemblée générale a voté le versement d'un dividende exceptionnel.
column7: The general meeting voted to pay an exceptional dividend.
column8: The share of profits distributed to shareholders; the noun is masculine.

column6: Un banquet réunira les anciens élèves à la fin de la cérémonie.
column7: A banquet will bring the alumni together at the end of the ceremony.
column8: A formal meal for many guests on an official occasion; more formal than «repas».

column6: Nous prenons le thé dans la véranda dès que le soleil revient.
column7: We have tea in the veranda as soon as the sun returns.
column8: In French it usually means a glazed room added to a house, not an open porch.

column6: Il présente un syndrome grippal accompagné de courbatures.
column7: He has flu-like symptoms accompanied by body aches.
column8: A group of symptoms that occur together; the noun is masculine.

column6: Aucun acte médical ne peut être pratiqué sans le consentement du patient.
column7: No medical act may be performed without the patient's consent.
column8: In bioethics one speaks of «consentement éclairé»: consent given after clear information.

column6: C'est un symptôme dont se plaignent fréquemment les patients stressés.
column7: It is a symptom that stressed patients frequently complain about.
column8: Spelled with «-emment» but pronounced [amɑ̃]. More formal than «souvent».
